title: Mode switch arrow keys threw in rAF; focus stayed on the unchecked radio
body:
## Summary
ModeSwitch read e.currentTarget inside a requestAnimationFrame callback; React nulls it after the listener, so every arrow press threw and focus never followed the checked radio.

## Description
apps/studio/src/components/finish.tsx ModeSwitch (5 surfaces: Front x3, apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapCell.tsx:205, apps/studio/src/routes/HeatmapFeasibility.tsx:208). react-dom 19.3 executeDispatch sets `event.currentTarget = null` after the listener returns, so `e.currentTarget.querySelector` in the frame callback threw TypeError; the old radio kept focus at tabIndex -1. accessibility/keyboard-navigation-models: arrows move the roving stop and the focus together. Fixed: modeKeyDown() captures the group synchronously.

## Flow
- focus the 'Line at' switch on the Front, press ArrowRight
- mode flips; the rAF callback reads null.currentTarget -> TypeError in the console
- focus stays on the now-unchecked radio (tabIndex -1)

## Expected impact
Keyboard users get focus on the checked option on all 5 switches; measured by finish.test.ts. Could break: nothing - same flip, same selector.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - arrow keys move focus to the checked radio without throwing
Before: 1/2 cases red with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'querySelector') (seeded on the extracted old body)
After: 2/2 green; focus lands on [data-mode=<next>]
Method: gate - finish.test.ts delivers the keydown the way React does (currentTarget nulled after the listener)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Front failure lines called an API that answered "offline"
body:
## Summary
Six Front failure sites said '(API offline)' / 'the API did not answer' under every error, while ui.tsx Failure already separates an answered error from no answer.

## Description
0bb3662 added api.ts serverAnswered() so Failure stops asking whether the API runs when it answered; the Front's inline lines (registry readout, rundown way, lanes, registry picture, first short, On the line) kept the blanket claim. async-ui-states/failure-states: state what is known; unreachable and rejected differ. Fixed: apps/studio/src/frontpf.ts loadCause() feeds all six.

## Flow
- the API answers JSON 500 {error: SQLITE_BUSY} for /api/sources
- the Front reads 'The registry did not answer (API offline)'
- the owner restarts a server that was up; the real reason is never shown

## Expected impact
The owner sees the API's own reason when it answered, and 'API offline' only when nothing did. Could break: copy only; e2e grepped clean.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - failure copy names the cause it has
Before: 6/6 sites asserted offline regardless of cause; loadCause seeded with the old rule: 1/2 red
After: 0/6; 2/2 green (3 no-answer shapes keep 'API offline', 2 answered shapes quote the API)
Method: gate - frontpf.test.ts loadCause cases mirroring ui.test.ts shapes
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: 9558d76; apps/studio/src/frontpf.ts loadCause; apps/studio/src/api.ts serverAnswered; residual apps/studio/src/components/OnTheLine.tsx:65 (partial line, no error object in workQuery.ts)

## Description

Fixed: Frame receives the heatmap query; apps/studio/src/frontpf.ts heatmapWay() picks loading / error (with loadCause) / empty / ready, held counts winning over a failed refetch. title: Lane art cache grew one drawing per mount (useId in the key)
body:
## Summary
LaneArt cached markup under `${id}|${useId}`; every client mount has a fresh useId and the lane stage remounts each 3.2 s rotation step, so a module Map grew without bound.

## Description
apps/studio/src/components/LaneArt.tsx markup() (before: key `${id}|${g}`); the Lanes stage is keyed `${u.id}-${stageKey}` (apps/studio/src/routes/FrontPhotoFinish.tsx Lanes). motion/performance-discipline: an idle loop must not cost more the longer it runs. Fixed: one drawing per use case built with a placeholder gradient id, filled per mount.

## Flow
- leave the Front's lanes in view
- the rotation remounts the stage every 3.2 s
- the cache gains ~4.2 K chars per step and never frees them

## Expected impact
Memory stays flat while the Front sits open. Could break: none - each mount still gets its own gradient id (tested).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - bounded drawing cache
Before: 50 mounts -> 50 entries (seeded red); average drawing 4,234 chars (tsx probe over 6 ids)
After: 50 mounts -> 1 entry; 2/2 green
Method: gate - LaneArt.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Defer marks a section shown at mount, so a revisit mounts below-fold work at once
body:
## Summary
arrive.tsx Defer adds its id to the session seen-set when it mounts, not when it reveals; a section never scrolled to counts as shown and mounts instantly on the next visit.

## Description
apps/studio/src/components/arrive.tsx:69 `if (id) shown.add(id)` runs before `if (ready) return`; :62 instant = shown.has(id). On the Front, pf:line and pf:short are `visible` Defers (apps/studio/src/routes/FrontPhotoFinish.tsx:138,149): on a second visit the first short mounts at once and, with props, imports the Remotion chunk the front-load-diet direction kept off the page. motion/one-shot-guarding: a seen-set records what was SEEN. Fix: add to the set when ready turns true.

## Flow
- open the Front, leave without scrolling
- come back
- pf:short mounts at once (no fade) and Programme imports the composition chunk

## Expected impact
Below-fold work waits for the scroll again on revisits. Could break: a revisited, never-shown section fades in once more.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - below-fold sections stay deferred on revisit
Before: walked: arrive.tsx adds to the seen-set before the ready check; 2 visible Defers on the Front
After: not measured
Method: simulation - the studio test env is node (vitest.config.ts environment: node), so effects cannot run; a jsdom/happy-dom dev dependency is a lockfile change (Class C, Director installs)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a DOM-capable test (per-file happy-dom env) mounting Defer(id, visible) twice without intersection: 2nd mount ready=true today, false after; or a Playwright count of composition-chunk requests on a second Front visit

title: The frame's slit-scan loop re-parses hex and reads computed style every frame
body:
## Summary
useScan's draw() reads getComputedStyle(documentElement).fontSize and regex-parses lane hex in rgba() ~1,000 times per frame, plus ~300 gradients, at 60 fps.

## Description
apps/studio/src/routes/FrontPhotoFinish.tsx:640 getComputedStyle per frame; :513 rgba() regex-parses its hex on every call (streak slices x gradient stops, ~144 ruler ticks); :665,672 createLinearGradient per slice. motion/performance-discipline. Fix: precompute rgb per lane and rem in layout(); build each streak's gradients once.

## Flow
- the Front is open on a desktop
- every animation frame: 1 style read, ~1,000 hex regex parses, ~300 gradients

## Expected impact
A cheaper hero animation on low-end machines. Could break: colours if the cache misses a token change (layout() re-reads on resize).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - per-frame cost of the hero canvas
Before: walked count: 8 streaks x 26 slices x 3-5 rgba + ~144 ruler ticks ~ 1,000 parses/frame
After: not measured
Method: simulation - a ms figure needs a browser performance trace; an S fake-ctx counter gives the call counts
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a fake CanvasRenderingContext2D counting rgba()/getComputedStyle/createLinearGradient per draw() on both arms, plus a 5 s Chrome trace of scripting time
